You are the implementing engineer for Atlas ERP, in '/Users/taha/Claude projects/expremental ERP/atlas-erp' on branch feat/quality-inspection (dev merged; core+finance+inventory+procurement+sales+manufacturing all complete). NO git commands. uv at ~/.local/bin/uv; run `cd backend && ~/.local/bin/uv run <cmd>`. PostgreSQL 16 at postgresql+asyncpg://atlas:atlas@localhost:55432/atlas (LOCAL — run the full pg suite).

This OPENS the quality module (sixth business module). Scope per the parity doc is DELIBERATELY SMALL: inspection flag on goods receipt → inspection lot → accept/reject with stock disposition. Everything else QM (inspection plans, usage-decision codes, results recording, quality notifications) is out of v1.

READ FIRST (binding): docs/research/s4hana-parity.md QM/PM section (the one FULL QM capability is "inspection flag on goods receipt → inspection lot → accept/reject with stock disposition"; inspection plans / usage decisions / notifications = out of scope); docs/architecture.md D-011 (event bus — quality subscribes to procurement's GoodsReceiptPosted to create inspection lots; multiple handlers on one event key is supported), D-020/D-045/D-048 (the offset-override + event-driven stock-move pattern — a REJECT disposition moves stock via the event bus), D-012/D-013/D-014/D-015/D-022/D-025/D-007/D-029. Then read the EXACT code:
- backend/app/modules/procurement/events.py (GoodsReceiptPosted — it already carries per-line item_id, quantity, bin, lot/serial, requires_inspection, and the GR document id; quality subscribes to it and creates an inspection lot per requires_inspection line) + procurement/models/goods_receipts.py (the GR line shape) + backend/app/modules/inventory/handlers.py (how the GoodsReceiptPosted handler creates RECEIPT moves — quality's handler runs ALONGSIDE it on the same event) + how handlers are registered in backend/app/main.py (register_event_handlers).
- backend/app/modules/inventory/service/stock_moves.py (create_move — a REJECT disposition is a stock ADJUSTMENT-out for scrap OR a TRANSFER to a blocked bin; decide below) + inventory/queries.py (bins, on_hand). The disposition stock effect goes via the EVENT BUS (quality publishes a disposition event → inventory/handlers.py moves the stock), per §5 (quality must NOT import inventory/finance service).
- backend/app/modules/manufacturing/ as the freshest module template (constants/models/schemas/service/queries/router packages, sibling-router mounting), and tests/modules/manufacturing/{factories.py, conftest.py} for the fixture pattern; plus tests/modules/procurement (to build a goods receipt that flags inspection).
Latest migration = 0034.

CRITICAL §5: quality must NOT import procurement/inventory/finance SERVICE. It SUBSCRIBES to procurement's GoodsReceiptPosted (importing procurement/events — sanctioned events import) and READS via queries; a reject disposition that scraps/blocks stock publishes a quality event → inventory/handlers.py performs the move. Confirm quality→procurement/events + quality→inventory/queries are one-directional (procurement/inventory don't import quality — they're older; no cycle). Document in DECISIONS D-050.

TASK — PLAN 9.1: quality inspection lots from goods receipts + accept/reject disposition. Build:

1. `backend/app/modules/quality/__init__.py`, `constants.py`:
   - Enums: InspectionLotStatus (OPEN|ACCEPTED|REJECTED|CANCELLED — OPEN on creation, ACCEPTED/REJECTED on usage decision), InspectionSource (GOODS_RECEIPT — the only v1 source; declare the enum for future sources but only GOODS_RECEIPT is used), RejectDisposition (SCRAP|RETURN_TO_VENDOR|BLOCK — what happens to rejected stock; v1 implement SCRAP (an inventory ADJUSTMENT-out writing the value off) and BLOCK (a TRANSFER to a designated blocked/QI bin); RETURN_TO_VENDOR can be declared but document it as a later if not implemented — prefer SCRAP + BLOCK implemented, RETURN_TO_VENDOR out).
   - Permissions: quality.inspection.read/.manage/.decide (decide = the accept/reject usage decision, distinct).
   - Number sequence 'quality.inspection_lot' (QL-… or INSP-). Doc type + docflow links goods-receipt→inspection-lot and inspection-lot→disposition-stock-move.
2. `backend/app/modules/quality/models.py` (or models/ if >400): `InspectionLot` (`qm_inspection_lots`): DocumentMixin header; lot_number, status, source (InspectionSource), source_document_id (the GR document id — opaque core_documents id, via docflow link rather than FK), item_id (opaque, from the GR line), quantity (QuantityType — inspected qty), bin_id (opaque — where the received stock is), lot_id/serial info (nullable, from the GR line), warehouse_id (opaque), created_date, decided_date (nullable), decision_by (user id nullable), disposition (RejectDisposition nullable — set on reject), accepted_quantity / rejected_quantity (QuantityType — a usage decision can split: some accepted, some rejected), notes. The inspection lot is created OPEN when a GR with requires_inspection posts.
3. `backend/app/modules/quality/events.py` (NEW): `InspectionRejected` (or `InspectionDispositioned`) carrying tenant_id, the inspection-lot document id, item_id, rejected_quantity, from_bin, lot/serial, disposition (SCRAP→ADJUSTMENT-out; BLOCK→TRANSFER to blocked bin — carry the target bin for BLOCK), the move_date — everything inventory/handlers.py needs to move the rejected stock. (Accepted stock needs NO move — it's already received and usable.)
4. `backend/app/modules/quality/handlers.py` (NEW): subscribe to procurement's GoodsReceiptPosted event key; for each line with requires_inspection=True, create an OPEN InspectionLot (claim QL number, link docflow GR→lot) in the SAME transaction as the GR post (the handler shares the session — so a flagged GR atomically creates its inspection lots). Register in app.main.register_event_handlers ALONGSIDE the inventory GR handler.
5. `backend/app/modules/quality/service.py` (or service/ package): 
   - list/get inspection lots; create_manual? (v1 source is GR-only via the handler; a manual create is optional — skip unless trivial; document GR is the source).
   - `decide(lot_id, accepted_quantity, rejected_quantity, disposition?)` — the usage decision (permission quality.inspection.decide), in run_in_uow: validate accepted + rejected == lot quantity (or ≤ with the remainder staying open? v1: a single decision covering the whole lot — accepted + rejected == quantity, else 422); if rejected > 0, require a disposition and PUBLISH the disposition event → inventory moves the rejected stock (SCRAP = ADJUSTMENT-out from the bin, posting the inventory write-off journal via the existing costing event with the price-difference/scrap offset; BLOCK = TRANSFER to the blocked bin, value-neutral). Set status ACCEPTED (rejected==0), REJECTED (accepted==0), or a partial (some of each — pick a status: if any rejected → REJECTED with accepted_quantity recorded, or a PARTIALLY_ACCEPTED status; keep it: ACCEPTED if rejected==0 else REJECTED, with both quantities recorded; document). decided_date/by set. Atomic; closed-period (the scrap journal) rolls back. Idempotent (a decided lot can't be re-decided). 
   - cancel an OPEN lot (no disposition).
6. `backend/app/modules/quality/queries.py`: get_inspection_lot, open_lots_for_item, lots_for_goods_receipt. The only imported file.
7. `backend/app/modules/quality/router.py`: GET /api/v1/quality/inspection-lots (paginated, filter status/item/source), GET /{id}, POST /{id}/decide (idempotent; quality.inspection.decide), POST /{id}/cancel. (No POST create — lots come from the GR handler; if you add a manual create, guard quality.inspection.manage.) Permission-guard; mount in main.py. PERFORMANCE §6.
8. Migration 0035_quality_inspection.py (down_revision 0034): qm_inspection_lots + indexes. No trigger-bearing alters.
9. docs/modules/quality.md: NEW module guide (the GR-flag→lot→decide→disposition flow, the event-driven lot creation, SCRAP/BLOCK dispositions + their stock effects, accepted-needs-no-move, what's out of scope per parity). DECISIONS.md D-050 (quality subscribes to procurement GoodsReceiptPosted to create lots; usage decision accept/reject with SCRAP (write-off) / BLOCK (transfer) dispositions via the event bus; accepted stock unchanged; the cross-module directions + no cycle).
10. Tests: test_inspection.py + test_inspection_api.py: a goods receipt with requires_inspection=True posts → an OPEN inspection lot is created (via the handler, in the same transaction; assert the lot exists with the right item/qty/bin and the GR→lot docflow link); a GR line WITHOUT the flag creates NO lot; decide ACCEPT (rejected=0) → status ACCEPTED, NO stock change (on-hand unchanged); decide REJECT with SCRAP → status REJECTED, an ADJUSTMENT-out move reduces on-hand + posts the write-off journal; decide REJECT with BLOCK → a TRANSFER to the blocked bin (total on-hand unchanged, moved out of the usable bin); partial accept/reject; accepted+rejected must equal lot qty (422 otherwise); re-decide rejected; cancel OPEN lot; closed-period disposition rolls back; RBAC (manage/decide), tenant isolation, pagination, ≤3 budgets. HEED issue #53 (don't assert post-failure state on the same session for handler-raised errors). Build the flagged GR via the procurement factories.

RULES: no TODO/stub/dead-file; absolute imports; ruff + pytest FULLY green SQLite (`-m "not pg and not perf"`) AND `-m pg` (reset pg schema, alembic upgrade head, run -m pg); delete stray atlas.db; every file <400 lines; comments only non-obvious; don't print file contents. Update PROGRESS.md + tick PLAN 9.1 + DECISIONS.md D-050. Run STRUCTURE §9 self-check (esp. §5 + no cycle) and report it.

Return: files created/changed, the GR→inspection-lot event mechanism + §5/no-cycle verification, the accept/reject + SCRAP/BLOCK disposition stock effects, the accepted-needs-no-move rationale, test counts (SQLite total+new, pg), migration number, §9 self-check, deviations.

===PARITY QM/PM===
5:**Methodology.** All twelve functional areas below were verified through live web research against current sources (SAP Help Portal, SAP Learning, SAP Community, SAP PRESS, and ERP consulting publications); no area was built from the embedded knowledge baseline alone. Five areas — Financial Accounting, Inventory Management & Warehousing, Quality Management & Plant Maintenance, Project System, and Cross-cutting platform concepts — supplemented web findings with embedded S/4HANA knowledge for specific subtopics or where source pages could not be fetched; these are flagged in the Sources appendix.
31:| Quality Management & Plant Maintenance (QM / PM-EAM) | 1 | 4 | 7 | 12 |
136:| **Returns processing (RMA / Advanced Returns Management)** | Full | sales | Later: Inspection dispositions, refund-determination rules, and vendor-return chains can be added on the RMA later. |
165:## Quality Management & Plant Maintenance (QM / PM-EAM)
167:In current S/4HANA (2025/2026), QM covers quality planning (inspection plans, master inspection characteristics, sampling), quality inspection (inspection lots auto-created at goods receipt, in production, and at delivery), characteristic-level results recording, coded usage decisions that drive stock postings out of quality-inspection stock, and quality notifications/CAPA, plus certificates and supplier quality. PM-EAM centers on technical objects (equipment installed on hierarchical functional locations), maintenance notifications feeding corrective maintenance orders with a phase-based lifecycle, preventive maintenance plans (time-, performance/counter-, and strategy-based) scheduled against task lists, and measurement points/counters for condition readings. Against the Atlas v1 plan, the GR-inspection-to-disposition flow, equipment register, and corrective/interval-based preventive orders cover a credible minimal core, but inspection plans, results recording, quality and maintenance notifications, functional locations, and measurement points are genuine gaps practitioners will notice.
171:| **Inspection lots** | Partial | quality | Only GR-origin lots via an inspection flag are planned; production/in-process, delivery, and manual lot origins plus sampling/sample-size logic are not. Later: Extend the existing lot object with additional origins (production order, delivery, manual) and sampling procedures. |
172:| **Inspection plans and master inspection characteristics** | Out of scope | — | Explicitly excluded from the v1 list; v1 lots are plan-less binary accept/reject with no characteristic or sampling master data. Later: Introduce inspection plan + characteristic master data and assign plans to lots at creation. |
173:| **Results recording** | Out of scope | — | Depends on inspection plans/characteristics, which are cut; v1 captures only a lot-level accept/reject outcome, not measured values. Later: After plans/characteristics exist, add a characteristic-level results entry screen with auto-valuation. |
174:| **Usage decisions with stock disposition** | Partial | quality | Binary accept/reject with a stock move is planned, but coded UD catalogs, quality scores, and split-quantity postings (scrap/sample/return) are not. Later: Add UD code catalogs and multi-bucket quantity split posting on top of the existing accept/reject action. |
175:| **Quality notifications (defects/complaints/CAPA)** | Out of scope | — | No defect/complaint workflow in v1; a rejected lot only moves stock and does not open a tracked quality issue. Later: Add a generic notification/issue object (shared with maintenance notifications) linkable to lots, suppliers, and materials. |
176:| Quality certificates and supplier quality | Out of scope | — | Not in the v1 plan; mainly needed in regulated industries and dependent on results recording, which is also cut. Later: Generate certificate documents from recorded results and add a vendor-material quality status check in procurement. |

===D-011===
3:This document is the implementation contract derived from the Phase-2 architecture review. Each section below is a numbered decision (D-007 … D-026), also indexed in [DECISIONS.md](../DECISIONS.md). Implementers must follow these mechanisms exactly — table names, API names, constraint semantics, trigger behavior, and parameter values are normative, not illustrative. Any change requires a superseding DECISIONS.md entry referencing the decision it replaces.
7:## D-007 — Tenancy enforcement (non-bypassable session filter)
142:## D-011 — Domain-event bus (collect-then-dispatch, in-transaction)
171:## D-012 — Document registry, flow links, and gapless numbering (merged)
209:## D-013 — Idempotency keys (reservation, atomic completion via route capture)
240:- Phase-1 real COMMIT requires the test harness to support genuine commits — satisfied by the per-test database-copy strategy (see D-025).

142	## D-011 — Domain-event bus (collect-then-dispatch, in-transaction)
143	
144	**Decision.**
145	`core/events.py` defines `DomainEvent` (frozen Pydantic v2 model, ClassVar `key` like `'sales.order.shipped'`, fields `tenant_id` + `occurred_at`), an `EventBus` Protocol with `publish(session, event)`, a `@subscribe(key)` decorator, and `InProcessEventBus`.
146	
147	**Semantics:** services call `bus.publish(session, event)`, which appends to a FIFO buffer in `session.info['pending_events']` — no immediate dispatch. The buffer is drained by ONE shared unit-of-work helper `run_in_uow()` in `core/db.py`, used both by the request session dependency in `core/deps.py` and by `seed.py`/CLI flows (so seed and HTTP get identical event semantics): after the service returns and before commit, pop events FIFO and run each handler synchronously, passing `(event, session)` so handlers write into the SAME transaction; handlers may publish further events appended to the same queue (breadth-first), with a hard cap of 50 dispatches per transaction raising `EventCycleError`.
148	
149	**Handler order is deterministic:** registration order = the fixed module import order in `main.py`'s app factory (finance, inventory, procurement, sales, …). Any handler exception propagates, the whole transaction rolls back, the API returns the error envelope — deliberately NO per-handler isolation: if the COGS posting fails, the goods issue must not commit.
150	
151	**Placement:** handlers live only in `modules/<m>/handlers.py` via `@subscribe` and import event classes from the publishing module's `events.py` — recorded in DECISIONS.md as an explicit STRUCTURE §5 amendment: `events.py` joins `queries.py` as a sanctioned cross-module import because it is declarative-only (Pydantic event definitions, no logic, no models); this also covers `finance/handlers.py` importing "upward" from `inventory/events.py`, which is acceptable precisely because `events.py` carries no behavior.
152	
153	**Audit interplay:** handler writes are captured by the audit flush listeners automatically since they share the session. Non-transactional side effects (email, webhooks) are banned from this bus; the seam for them is a later after-commit hook, recorded now in DECISIONS.md. **Swap path:** a future `TransactionalOutboxBus` implements the same Protocol, writing `core_event_outbox` rows (key + JSON payload) in the same transaction for a relay — zero module changes.
154	
155	**Rationale.**
156	Dispatch-in-transaction is the only semantics upholding CLAUDE.md rules 6+8: cross-module financial effects (goods issue → COGS journal) must be all-or-nothing with their trigger, and a sync in-process bus sharing the session gives exactly-once atomic causality with no outbox machinery in v1. Buffering until the service returns means handlers observe settled aggregate state. Deterministic ordering makes ledger line order and test output reproducible. The single `run_in_uow` drain point closes the gap where seed-created documents would otherwise skip COGS/docflow side effects.
157	
158	**Rejected alternatives.**
159	- After-commit dispatch: a crashed handler leaves shipped stock with no COGS posting and no remediation — unacceptable without outbox+retry, which is post-v1.
160	- Publish-time immediate dispatch: handlers interleave with the publisher's half-finished writes.
161	- Per-handler catch-and-continue: converts consistency bugs into silent divergence.
162	- Celery/background handlers: loses the transaction and adds forbidden infrastructure.
163	- String-key-only events without importable classes: loses typing for no architectural gain since `events.py` is declarative.
164	
165	**Risks & mitigations.**
166	- Long synchronous chains extend transaction hold time (numbering row locks, SQLite writer lock) — bounded by the depth cap, thin handlers (post + publish only, no external I/O), and a per-dispatch debug log.
167	- A handler needing foreign-module data must use that module's `queries.py`, never the session against foreign models — enforced by import linting in CI.
168	
169	---
170	
171	## D-012 — Document registry, flow links, and gapless numbering (merged)
172	
173	**Decision.**
174	One subsystem in `core/docflow.py` + `core/numbering.py`, because registration timing and number claiming are inseparable.
175	
176	**Registry `core_documents`:** id uuid PK, tenant_id, doc_type (namespaced constant like `'sales.order'`, `'fin.journal_entry'`, declared in module `constants.py` and collected in a core registry), doc_no text NULLABLE, status, created_at; partial unique index on (tenant_id, doc_type, doc_no) declared with BOTH `postgresql_where=doc_no.isnot(None)` and `sqlite_where=...` (partial indexes work on both engines but each needs its dialect kwarg); UNIQUE(tenant_id, id) to serve composite tenant FKs. Every business document table carries `document_id uuid NOT NULL UNIQUE` FK via `DocumentMixin`, created by `docflow.register(session, doc_type, doc_no=None)` in the creating service.
177	
178	**Edges `core_doc_links`:** predecessor_id/successor_id FK → `core_documents.id`, link_type (`'fulfills'`, `'invoices'`, `'reverses'`, `'posts'`), nullable quantity/amount/currency_code for partial fulfillment, PK(predecessor_id, successor_id, link_type), CHECK(predecessor_id != successor_id), tenant composite-FK pattern.
179	
180	**Traversal:** `docflow.get_chain` runs one recursive CTE per direction (`select().cte(recursive=True)`, works on PG and SQLite), depth column capped at 20, visited-path cycle guard; `GET /api/v1/core/documents/{id}/flow` returns `{nodes, edges}` for DocFlowViewer; display extras come from per-doc_type summary callbacks modules register.
181	
182	**Numbering:** `core_number_sequences` (tenant_id, doc_type, year int — 0 for non-resetting, prefix, pattern, next_no, padding; PK(tenant_id, doc_type, year)). `next_document_number(session, doc_type, year=None)`:
183	1. `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (PG and SQLite >=3.24);
184	2. atomic `UPDATE ... SET next_no = next_no + 1 WHERE ... RETURNING next_no - 1, prefix, pattern, padding` (RETURNING on PG and SQLite >=3.35; a tested SELECT-then-UPDATE fallback exists, safe under SQLite's single-writer lock);
185	3. format via pattern, validated at write time against a `{prefix}/{year}/{seq}` field whitelist.
186	
187	**Claim-timing rule** (fixes the draft conflict between gaplessness and draft documents): a number is claimed in the transaction that makes the document PERMANENT. Documents with a draft lifecycle (journal entries) are registered with doc_no NULL at creation and numbered via `docflow.assign_number(session, document_id)` inside the posting transaction; documents permanent at creation (orders, receipts, invoices) are numbered at creation; once numbered, a document is never hard-deleted — cancellation is a status — so gaplessness is a free consequence of ACID (claim and document commit or roll back together). The registry's partial unique index is the DB backstop turning any numbering bug into a constraint violation.
188	
189	Registry status is updated only via `docflow.set_status()` in the owning transaction; a reconciliation assertion runs in tests. Year rollover needs no job: the first posting of a new year inserts the new counter row on demand.
190	
191	**Rationale.**
192	The registry turns the polymorphic (doc_type, doc_id) problem into ordinary FK integrity and makes chain traversal one generic CTE over one narrow table — the ACDOCA-era Document Relationship Browser shape. Merging numbering in fixes a real hole: the original drafts simultaneously required NOT NULL document numbers at creation and gapless counters, which means every abandoned draft journal entry burns a number; nullable doc_no + claim-at-permanence resolves it without weakening either invariant. The hot-row UPDATE is the textbook portable gapless pattern: counter increment and document are atomic, so there is no burned-number state to reconcile.
193	
194	**Rejected alternatives.**
195	- Bare polymorphic (doc_type, doc_id) link pairs: no FK enforcement, per-type join fan-out.
196	- Per-table FK links only: chain traversal needs N module-aware queries in core, violating core-imports-nothing.
197	- Postgres SEQUENCE/SERIAL: non-transactional (gaps by design), not per-tenant, nonexistent on SQLite.
198	- `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` for the counter: the bare atomic UPDATE achieves the same row lock in one portable statement.
199	- Separate draft number ranges: two numbering semantics to explain and audit.
200	- Materialized closure table: premature, chains are <10 nodes.
201	
202	**Risks & mitigations.**
203	- Dual-write discipline (business row + registry + links in one transaction) — mitigated by `DocumentMixin`'s NOT NULL document_id (insert fails without registration) and a shared test helper asserting chain integrity per module happy path.
204	- The counter row serializes concurrent posting of one doc_type per tenant — milliseconds at v1 scale; the documented later path (cached ranges for non-legal doc_types) only changes `numbering.py`.
205	- Convention: claim numbers as late as possible in the service to shorten lock hold.
206	
207	---

209	## D-013 — Idempotency keys (reservation, atomic completion via route capture)
210	
211	**Decision.**
212	Table `core_idempotency_keys`: tenant_id, key (client `Idempotency-Key` header, max 200 chars), endpoint (METHOD + route template), request_hash (sha256 of canonical JSON body), status (`'in_progress'`|`'completed'`), response_status int nullable, response_body JSON nullable, created_at, completed_at; PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, endpoint, key).
213	
214	**Two-phase flow** with an explicit fix to the draft's broken epilogue (a FastAPI dependency can never see the route's serialized response, and writing 'completed' after commit would break atomicity):
215	
216	- **Phase 1.** The `idempotency_guard()` dependency in `core/deps.py` opens a SEPARATE short-lived session from the sessionmaker, INSERTs the (tenant, endpoint, key, request_hash, 'in_progress') row and COMMITs immediately so concurrent duplicates collide on the PK (PG unique index arbitrates; SQLite's single-writer lock serializes). On conflict it reads the existing row:

54:- **D-048 Production orders (PLAN 8.2): reserve → issue components to WIP (Dr WIP / Cr Inventory) → finish to stock (Dr Inventory / Cr WIP) through the EVENT BUS with a valuation-offset OVERRIDE to a WIP clearing account; WIP nets to ZERO per fully-issued+finished order; accumulated_wip_cost tracked on the order; residual flushes to a production-variance account; single-level explosion per order:** A production order (`mfg_production_orders`, prefix `MO-` — distinct from purchase-order `PO-`) turns components into a finished parent item across the manufacturing↔inventory↔finance seam, mirroring the 6.3 GR/IR override and 7.3 delivery COGS. Routing the variance through a finance HANDLER (a second OrderFinished subscriber) — not a manufacturing-posted journal — keeps manufacturing free of any finance/service import (§5). The existing inventory→finance StockValued handler posts both WIP journals unchanged (it is a generic Dr/Cr switch over the event's offset). **(g) Over-issue/closed-period.** v1 over-issue policy: issued ≤ required (beyond → 422 `manufacturing.over_issue`). 7	GR/IR clearing account (so the move credits GR/IR); a delivery passes NO override, because an ISSUE
8	move's DEFAULT valuation offset IS the item-category COGS account (the costing engine routes an

10	the issue offset.

13	the SAME transaction as the GR post (D-011 run_in_uow drains before commit). This is the SANCTIONED
14	cross-module mechanism (STRUCTURE §5): procurement must NOT import inventory's service, so the GR
15	post publishes ``GoodsReceiptPosted`` (a plain typed event — the only procurement file this handler
16	imports) and inventory reacts by calling its OWN ``stock_moves.create_move``. The mirror of the
17	existing inventory→finance pattern (inventory publishes StockValued, finance/handlers posts the
18	journal) — here procurement publishes, inventory handles.
19

142	    stock enters at, > 0). An ISSUE / negative ADJUSTMENT / TRANSFER IGNORE any passed cost — the
143	    engine computes the outbound cost / carries the current valuation — so the move stores it as
144	    None
145	    and the engine fills it. Returns the validated entry cost (None for the computed sides)."""
146	    if _is_inbound(move_type, payload.to_bin_id):
147	        if payload.unit_cost is None or Decimal(payload.unit_cost) <= 0:
148	            raise ValidationFailedError(

150	                code="inventory.receipt_unit_cost_required",

167	    concurrent movers touching the same pair lock it in the same order). A decrement raises
168	    InsufficientStockError if it would go negative (no-negative-stock, D-020)."""
169	    deltas: list[tuple[uuid.UUID, Decimal]] = []
170	    if from_bin_id is not None:

172	    if to_bin_id is not None:
173	        deltas.append((to_bin_id, quantity))
174	    # Lock/update in ascending bin-id order so two concurrent transfers between the same bins
175	    # never deadlock by locking the pair in opposite orders (D-020 deadlock avoidance).
176	    for bin_id, delta in sorted(deltas, key=lambda pair: pair[0].bytes):
177	        await apply_bin_delta(session, tenant_id, item_id, bin_id, lot_id, delta)

180	async def create_move(
181	    session: AsyncSession,
182	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
183	    payload: StockMoveCreate,
184	    *,
185	    reversal_of: StockMove | None = None,
186	    valuation_offset_account_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
187	) -> StockMove:
188	    """Create + POST a stock move (the heart, PLAN 5.2/5.3). Validates everything (see module
189	    docstring), claims the gapless STK number, inserts the POSTED move, updates the quant
190	    projection, runs COSTING and publishes the valuation event — all in ONE transaction (D-020). 422
191	    InsufficientStockError when an issue/transfer exceeds on-hand; NotFound for a missing item; 422
192	    for a non-stocked item or a bin-side rule break. The caller commits via uow.
193	
194	    ``reversal_of`` (set by ``reverse_move``) runs the costing REVERSAL path: the reversing move
195	    replays the original's FIFO consumptions / re-applies its moving-average value and emits the
196	    OPPOSITE valuation event so the COGS journal is reversed too (D-020).
197	
198	    ``valuation_offset_account_id`` (PLAN 6.3, D-041) OVERRIDES the receipt's standard
199	    valuation-offset (price-difference): the procurement goods-receipt path passes the GR/IR
200	    clearing account, so the StockValued event carries it as ``offset_account_id`` and the finance
201	    handler credits GR/IR. Ignored on non-receipt types and on a reversal. None ⇒ unchanged."""
202	    move_type = MoveType(payload.move_type)
203	    quantity = Decimal(payload.quantity)
204	    if quantity <= 0:
205	        raise ValidationFailedError(
206	            message="Move quantity must be greater than zero",
207	            code="inventory.move_quantity_invalid",
208	            details={"quantity": str(quantity)},
209	        )
210	
211	    item = await _require_stocked_item(session, tenant_id, payload.item_id)
212	    _validate_bin_sides(move_type, payload.from_bin_id, payload.to_bin_id)
213	    # Costing input (D-020): a RECEIPT/positive-ADJUSTMENT requires the entry cost; computed sides
214	    # ignore it. Validated BEFORE any write so a missing cost fails fast (no number burned). A
215	    # reversal carries its cost from the original move (the costing reversal path), so it does not
216	    # need (and does not pass) an entry cost — skip the requirement.
217	    entry_cost = None if reversal_of is not None else _validate_unit_cost(payload, move_type)
218	    if payload.from_bin_id is not None:
219	        await _require_active_bin(session, tenant_id, payload.from_bin_id, side="from")
220	    if payload.to_bin_id is not None:
221	        await _require_active_bin(session, tenant_id, payload.to_bin_id, side="to")
222	
223	    # A receipt MAY create a lot/serial master instance (5.1 deferred that to receipts); an
224	    # issue/transfer/adjustment-decrease must reference one that already exists with stock.
225	    create_instance = move_type == MoveType.RECEIPT
226	    lot_id = await resolve_lot(
227	        session,
228	        tenant_id,
229	        item,
230	        lot_id=payload.lot_id,
231	        lot_code=payload.lot_code,
232	        create_if_missing=create_instance,
233	    )
234	    serial_id = await resolve_serial(
235	        session,
236	        tenant_id,
237	        item,
238	        serial_id=payload.serial_id,
239	        serial_code=payload.serial_code,
240	        create_if_missing=create_instance,
241	    )
242	    if TrackingMode(item.tracking_mode) == TrackingMode.SERIAL and quantity != 1:
243	        raise ValidationFailedError(
244	            message="A serial-tracked move has quantity 1 (a serial moves wholesale)",
245	            code="inventory.serial_quantity_invalid",
246	            details={"quantity": str(quantity)},
247	        )
248	
249	    move_date = payload.move_date or date.today()
250	    move_id = uuid.uuid4()
251	    document = await docflow.register_document(
252	        session,
253	        tenant_id,
254	        STOCK_MOVE_DOC_TYPE,
255	        move_id,
256	        doc_number=None,
257	        status=MoveStatus.POSTED.value,
258	    )
259	    # A move is permanent at creation (POSTED immediately), so the number is claimed now (D-012
260	    # claim-at-permanence, the orders/receipts branch, not the draft branch).
261	    await ensure_sequence(
262	        session,
263	        tenant_id,
264	        STOCK_MOVE_SEQUENCE_NAME,
265	        STOCK_MOVE_NUMBER_PREFIX,
266	        STOCK_MOVE_NUMBER_PADDING,
267	        year_reset=True,
268	    )
269	    move_number = await claim_number(
270	        session, tenant_id, STOCK_MOVE_SEQUENCE_NAME, on_date=move_date
271	    )
272	
273	    move = StockMove(
274	        id=move_id,
275	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
276	        document_id=document.id,
277	        move_number=move_number,
278	        move_type=move_type.value,
279	        item_id=item.id,
280	        quantity=quantity,
281	        base_uom_id=item.base_uom_id,
282	        from_bin_id=payload.from_bin_id,
283	        to_bin_id=payload.to_bin_id,
284	        lot_id=lot_id,
285	        serial_id=serial_id,
286	        move_date=move_date,
287	        reference=payload.reference,
288	        posted=True,
289	        # The validated entry cost on an inbound move; the costing engine fills the computed cost on

293	    session.add(move)

296	    await docflow.set_document_status(
297	        session, tenant_id, document.id, doc_number=move_number, status=MoveStatus.POSTED.value
298	    )
299	    await _apply_quant_deltas(
300	        session,
301	        tenant_id,
302	        item.id,
303	        lot_id,
304	        payload.from_bin_id,
305	        payload.to_bin_id,
306	        quantity,
307	    )
308	    # Costing IN THE SAME TRANSACTION (D-020), right after the quant update: update the
309	    # valuation/layers, write the computed cost onto the move, and publish StockValued BEFORE the
310	    # uow drains it — so move + quant + valuation + journal commit or roll back as one. A
311	    # value-neutral within-warehouse transfer returns no event (no journal).
312	    if reversal_of is not None:
313	        result = await costing_reversal.reverse_costing(
314	            session, tenant_id, item, move, reversal_of
315	        )
316	    else:

318	            session, tenant_id, item, move,

320	        )
321	    if result.event is not None:
322	        publish(session, result.event)

326	async def reverse_move(
327	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, move_id: uuid.UUID
328	) -> StockMove:
329	    """Reverse a posted move by posting an OPPOSITE move (PLAN 5.2): same item/quantity/lot/serial
330	    with from_bin and to_bin SWAPPED, linked to the original via docflow ('reverses'). The ledger
331	    stays append-only — corrections are new moves, never edits (D-017 philosophy). The reversing
332	    move restores the quants the original changed; a reversal that would itself go negative (the
333	    stock already left) raises InsufficientStockError like any other move. A move may be reversed
334	    once (a second reverse of the same original is rejected)."""
335	    original = await get_move(session, tenant_id, move_id)
336	    # Guard against double-reversal: a reversing move points back via docflow 'reverses'. Cheap
337	    # check — has any move already reversed this one?
338	    if await _already_reversed(session, tenant_id, original.document_id):
339	        raise ConflictError(
340	            message="This stock move has already been reversed",
341	            code="inventory.move_already_reversed",
342	        )
343	
344	    reversal_payload = StockMoveCreate(
345	        move_type=MoveType(original.move_type),
346	        item_id=original.item_id,
347	        quantity=Decimal(original.quantity),
348	        # Swap the directions so the reversing move undoes the original's quant deltas.
349	        from_bin_id=original.to_bin_id,
350	        to_bin_id=original.from_bin_id,
351	        lot_id=original.lot_id,
352	        serial_id=original.serial_id,
353	        move_date=date.today(),
354	        reference=f"Reversal of {original.move_number}",
355	    )
356	    # A reversal of a RECEIPT swaps to an ISSUE-shaped move (from set, to NULL) and vice versa; for
357	    # ADJUSTMENT/TRANSFER the swap stays the same move_type. The bin-side validator accepts the
358	    # swapped shape because the move_type's required side follows the populated bin.
359	    reversal_payload = _retype_for_reversal(reversal_payload, MoveType(original.move_type))
360	
361	    # Pass the original so create_move runs the costing REVERSAL (replay), not a fresh valuation,
362	    # and
363	    # publishes the OPPOSITE StockValued event so the COGS journal is reversed in the same
364	    # transaction (D-020).
365	    reversal = await create_move(
366	        session, tenant_id, reversal_payload, reversal_of=original
367	    )
368	    await docflow.link_documents(
369	        session,
370	        tenant_id,
371	        predecessor=original.document_id,
372	        successor=reversal.document_id,
373	        link_type=STOCK_MOVE_REVERSES_LINK,
374	    )
375	    return reversal
376	
377	
378	def _retype_for_reversal(payload: StockMoveCreate, original_type: MoveType) -> StockMoveCreate:
379	    """A RECEIPT reverses as an ISSUE and an ISSUE as a RECEIPT (the bin sides flip, so the type
380	    must too, or the bin-side validator rejects the swapped shape). TRANSFER and ADJUSTMENT keep
381	    their type — a swapped TRANSFER is still a TRANSFER, and a swapped ADJUSTMENT (the single side
382	    moves to the other side) is still an ADJUSTMENT."""
383	    if original_type == MoveType.RECEIPT:
384	        return payload.model_copy(update={"move_type": MoveType.ISSUE})
385	    if original_type == MoveType.ISSUE:
386	        return payload.model_copy(update={"move_type": MoveType.RECEIPT})
387	    return payload
388	
389	
390	async def _already_reversed(
391	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, document_id: uuid.UUID
392	) -> bool:
393	    """Whether a 'reverses' edge already points FROM this move's document (it has been reversed)."""
394	    chain = await docflow.get_document_chain(session, tenant_id, document_id)
395	    return any(
396	        edge.link_type == STOCK_MOVE_REVERSES_LINK
397	        and edge.predecessor_document_id == document_id
398	        for edge in chain.edges
399	    )

309	    # StockValued for the finance handler above — a two-hop same-transaction chain
310	    # (procurement → inventory → finance).
311	    if receive_goods_receipt_moves not in handlers_for(GoodsReceiptPosted.key):
312	        subscribe(GoodsReceiptPosted.key, receive_goods_receipt_moves)
313	    # Sales delivery → inventory stock-move bridge (PLAN 7.3, D-045): the OUTBOUND twin of the GR
314	    # bridge — inventory's handler creates the ISSUE moves (Dr COGS / Cr Inventory, COGS the default
315	    # issue offset — no override) when a delivery posts, which in turn publish StockValued for the
316	    # finance handler above — the same two-hop same-transaction chain (sales → inventory → finance).
317	    if issue_delivery_moves not in handlers_for(DeliveryShipped.key):
318	        subscribe(DeliveryShipped.key, issue_delivery_moves)
319	    # Procurement invoice-match → finance AP-bill bridge (PLAN 6.4, D-042): finance's handler
320	    # creates + posts the matched vendor bill (Dr GR/IR + PPV / Cr AP) when a match posts, clearing
321	    # the GR/IR account the goods receipt credited — closing the procure-to-pay loop. Procurement
322	    # publishes; finance handles its own bill posting (STRUCTURE §5).
323	    if create_bill_for_match not in handlers_for(InvoiceMatched.key):
324	        subscribe(InvoiceMatched.key, create_bill_for_match)
325	    # Sales billing → finance AR-invoice bridge (PLAN 7.4, D-046): the MIRROR of the invoice-match →
326	    # AP-bill bridge, sign-flipped — finance's handler creates + posts the AR customer invoice (Dr
327	    # AR
328	    # control / Cr revenue + tax) when a billing posts. Sales publishes; finance handles its own
329	    # invoice posting (STRUCTURE §5).

331	        subscribe(BillingInvoiced.key, create_invoice_for_billing)
332	    # Sales return → inventory RECEIPT bridge (PLAN 7.4, D-046): inventory's handler receives the
333	    # goods back (Dr Inventory / Cr COGS via the COGS-offset override — reversing the delivery's
334	    # issue) when a return posts, which publishes StockValued for the finance COGS handler above.
335	    if receive_return_moves not in handlers_for(ReturnReceived.key):
336	        subscribe(ReturnReceived.key, receive_return_moves)
337	    # Sales return → finance AR-credit-note bridge (PLAN 7.4, D-046): finance's handler creates +
338	    # posts the AR credit note (Dr revenue / Cr AR + reverse tax — reversing the billing) when a
339	    # return posts. The second leg of an atomic return post (the first is the stock receipt above).
340	    if create_credit_note_for_return not in handlers_for(ReturnCredited.key):
341	        subscribe(ReturnCredited.key, create_credit_note_for_return)
342	    # Manufacturing production-order → inventory stock-move bridges (PLAN 8.2, D-048), the
343	    # manufacturing↔inventory↔finance seam. A component ISSUE posts Dr WIP / Cr Inventory (the
344	    # valuation-offset OVERRIDE to the WIP account — the 6.3 GR/IR-override pattern applied to an

352	    # RECEIPT move (Dr Inventory / Cr WIP) and finance's handler posts the residual WIP variance (so
353	    # WIP nets to zero). Both drain in the finish's uow; either failure rolls the whole finish back.

1	"""Manufacturing constants (STRUCTURE §3): the BOM/routing status enums and the permission keys,
2	registered into the core RBAC catalog at import (D-009).
3	
4	A SINGLE file (STRUCTURE §8.4: split into a constants/ package only at the 400-line cap, the
5	inventory precedent) — PLAN 8.1's masters sit well under that. Production orders (8.2) and MRP (8.3)
6	will add their own document types / number sequences / event keys; if that pushes this past the cap
7	it becomes a constants/ package then, the sales precedent.
8	
9	IDENTITY + NUMBERING (decided here, D-047). Manufacturing MASTERS carry no gapless document number:
10	
11	- **Work centres** and the BOM/routing CODE-bearing identity follow the master-data precedent
12	  (item_code / vendor_code / customer_code): ``work_center_code`` is USER-SUPPLIED and unique per
13	  tenant (``UNIQUE(tenant_id, code)``). A code, not a gapless number.
14	- **A BOM is identified by ``(item_id, version)``** — the item it PRODUCES plus a user-supplied
15	  version string — NOT a standalone code, mirroring S/4HANA's "BOM is keyed by material + BOM
16	  usage/alternative". ``UNIQUE(tenant_id, item_id, version)``. The same shape is used for routings
17	  for consistency: a routing is ``(item_id, version)`` too (NOT a routing_code), so BOM and routing
18	  identity read identically and a routing can be looked up the same way a BOM is.
19	
20	There is deliberately NO auto-sequence here: a master carries a stable user-chosen handle, never a
21	gapless number. The PRODUCTION ORDERS in 8.2 WILL register documents and claim a gapless number (a
22	posted document in the D-012 sense) — but the masters do not.
23	
24	ACTIVATION MODEL (D-047). A BOM/routing version has a lifecycle status (DRAFT|ACTIVE|INACTIVE):
25	
26	- **DRAFT** — editable: components/operations may be added, changed and removed. A new version is
27	  born DRAFT.
28	- **ACTIVE** — usable by production/MRP and FROZEN: its components/operations can no longer be
29	  changed (corrections are a NEW version, the append-only-master philosophy). At most ONE
30	  ACTIVE+``is_default`` version per item — the one ``get_active_bom_for_item`` /
31	  ``get_active_routing_for_item`` resolve (8.2/8.3 read this). Activating a version that becomes the
32	  new default first demotes the previously-default ACTIVE version's ``is_default`` flag.
33	- **INACTIVE** — retired: a once-ACTIVE version superseded by a newer one; kept for history /
34	  referenceability, never deleted.
35	
36	"MULTI-LEVEL via references" (D-047). The SCHEMA is single-level-per-BOM: a ``Bom`` header lists the
37	DIRECT components of one parent item. "Multi-level" emerges because a component item can itself be
38	the parent of its OWN ``Bom`` — the tree is resolved by EXPLOSION at MRP time (8.3), which walks
39	component item -> its active BOM -> its components recursively. A direct self-component (a component
40	whose item IS the BOM's parent) is rejected at the masters here; deeper cycle prevention (A needs B
41	needs A) is a 8.3 explosion-time concern (the explosion carries a visited set + depth cap, the
42	docflow get_chain precedent), not enforceable on a single-level row.
43	"""
44	
45	from enum import StrEnum
46	
47	from app.core.rbac import register_permissions
48	
49	
50	class ProductionOrderStatus(StrEnum):
51	    """Lifecycle of a PRODUCTION ORDER (PLAN 8.2, D-048). A production order turns components into a
52	    finished parent item; its status tracks the issue→finish progress.
53	
54	    Transitions (the service owns them, CLAUDE.md rule 7):
55	
56	    - **DRAFT** — created + the active BOM EXPLODED into reserved component rows (and the routing
57	      snapshotted into order operations). Editable only via cancel; releasing moves it forward.
58	    - **RELEASED** — materials are reserved (the component rows ARE the reservation, v1 ATP-style —
59	      release does NOT block on availability, only optionally flags shortages). Ready to issue.
60	    - **IN_PROGRESS** — at least one component has been issued to WIP (Dr WIP / Cr Inventory). The
61	      order is mid-production: it can issue more components or finish.
62	    - **FINISHED** — the parent item has been fully produced to stock (Dr Inventory / Cr WIP) and
63	      the ordered quantity is met. Terminal; WIP nets to zero (issue debits = finished credit +
64	      variance flush).
65	    - **CANCELLED** — abandoned before any component issued (DRAFT/RELEASED only). Once components
66	      are issued the order is POSTED-ish: it must be FINISHED (a future phase adds reversal), never
67	      cancelled, so issued stock + WIP never strand. Terminal.
68	    """
69	
70	    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
71	    RELEASED = "RELEASED"
72	    IN_PROGRESS = "IN_PROGRESS"
73	    FINISHED = "FINISHED"
74	    CANCELLED = "CANCELLED"
75	
76	
77	class PlannedOrderType(StrEnum):
78	    """How a PLANNED ORDER's net requirement is sourced (PLAN 8.3, D-049). The MAKE-vs-BUY rule is
79	    structural: an item is MAKE if it has an ACTIVE default BOM (it is produced in-house, and the
80	    run EXPLODES its BOM into dependent component demand), else BUY (it is procured — a leaf the
81	    explosion stops at).
82	
83	    - MAKE: convert → a real production order (manufacturing.create_production_order, intra-module).
84	    - BUY: convert → a procurement DRAFT requisition (cross-module, via the planned-buy query
85	      procurement reads — the §5-clean mechanism, D-049).
86	    """
87	
88	    MAKE = "MAKE"
89	    BUY = "BUY"
90	
91	
92	class PlannedOrderStatus(StrEnum):
93	    """Lifecycle of a PLANNED ORDER (PLAN 8.3, D-049). The MRP run produces PLANNED proposals; a
94	    planner FIRMS the ones to keep, CONVERTS them into real orders, or CANCELS them.
95	
96	    - PLANNED: the run's fresh proposal. SUPERSEDED by the next run (a re-run deletes un-firmed
97	      PLANNED orders and regenerates — the regeneration policy, D-049).
98	    - FIRMED: a planner has committed to it; a re-run KEEPS it (and nets it as supply, so it is not
99	      re-proposed). Editable into CONVERTED/CANCELLED.
100	    - CONVERTED: turned into a real production order / requisition (``converted_document_id`` links
101	      it via docflow). Terminal; a re-run keeps it and nets the created supply.
102	    - CANCELLED: a planner discarded it. Terminal; a re-run keeps the row (history) but it adds no
103	      supply.
104	    """
105	
106	    PLANNED = "PLANNED"
107	    FIRMED = "FIRMED"
108	    CONVERTED = "CONVERTED"
109	    CANCELLED = "CANCELLED"
110	
111	
112	class MrpRunStatus(StrEnum):
113	    """Lifecycle of an MRP RUN (PLAN 8.3, D-049) — distinct from the generic ``JobStatus`` because
114	    the run is a domain document with its own number, even when executed as a background job.
115	
116	    - RUNNING: the engine is gathering demand/supply and writing planned orders.
117	    - COMPLETED: the plan is written (planned-make/buy counts populated, ``completed_at`` set).
118	    - FAILED: the run aborted; no plan was committed (the uow rolled back).
119	    """
120	
121	    RUNNING = "RUNNING"
122	    COMPLETED = "COMPLETED"
123	    FAILED = "FAILED"
124	
125	
126	class BomStatus(StrEnum):
127	    """Lifecycle of a BOM VERSION (D-047). A BOM is activated to become usable by production/MRP.
128	
129	    - DRAFT: editable — components may be added/changed/removed. A new version starts here.
130	    - ACTIVE: usable by 8.2/8.3 and FROZEN — components are immutable; at most one ACTIVE+default
131	      version per item (the one MRP/production resolve).
132	    - INACTIVE: retired — a superseded version, kept for history, never deleted.
133	    """
134	
135	    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
136	    ACTIVE = "ACTIVE"
137	    INACTIVE = "INACTIVE"
138	
139	
140	class RoutingStatus(StrEnum):
141	    """Lifecycle of a ROUTING VERSION (D-047) — the routing twin of ``BomStatus``, identical
142	    semantics so BOM and routing activation read the same:
143	
144	    - DRAFT: editable — operations may be added/changed/removed.
145	    - ACTIVE: usable by 8.2/8.3 and FROZEN — operations are immutable; at most one ACTIVE+default
146	      version per item.
147	    - INACTIVE: retired — kept for history, never deleted.
148	    """
149	
150	    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
151	    ACTIVE = "ACTIVE"
152	    INACTIVE = "INACTIVE"
153	
154	
155	# --- Permissions (D-009): one key per guarded endpoint action -----------------
156	# read vs manage on each of the three masters. "manage" covers create/edit/activate/deactivate —
157	# activation is part of authoring a BOM/routing, not a separate privileged posting like
158	# journal.post (a BOM activation drives no GL effect), so it rides the manage key rather than its
159	# own. A separate key can be carved out later if activation needs segregation-of-duties.
160	MFG_BOM_READ = "manufacturing.bom.read"
161	MFG_BOM_MANAGE = "manufacturing.bom.manage"
162	MFG_WORKCENTER_READ = "manufacturing.workcenter.read"
163	MFG_WORKCENTER_MANAGE = "manufacturing.workcenter.manage"
164	MFG_ROUTING_READ = "manufacturing.routing.read"
165	MFG_ROUTING_MANAGE = "manufacturing.routing.manage"
166	
167	# Production-order permissions (PLAN 8.2, D-048). Three authorities at a sensible granularity:
168	# - ``.manage`` — create+explode, edit (cancel a draft) the order document (the masters' manage
169	#   precedent; no GL effect, like a delivery DRAFT).
170	# - ``.release`` — reserve materials (DRAFT→RELEASED). A distinct authority because committing
171	#   capacity/material is a planning decision separate from authoring the order.
172	# - ``.execute`` — issue components (Dr WIP / Cr Inventory) AND finish to stock (Dr Inventory / Cr
173	#   WIP). Issue + finish are folded under ONE key (both POST stock + journals — the shop-floor
174	#   action), the way a delivery's stock-issuing post is one ``.post`` right; segregating issue from
175	#   finish further is a later if a tenant needs it.
176	MFG_PRODUCTION_ORDER_READ = "manufacturing.production_order.read"
177	MFG_PRODUCTION_ORDER_MANAGE = "manufacturing.production_order.manage"
178	MFG_PRODUCTION_ORDER_RELEASE = "manufacturing.production_order.release"
179	MFG_PRODUCTION_ORDER_EXECUTE = "manufacturing.production_order.execute"
180	
181	# MRP + planned-order permissions (PLAN 8.3, D-049). The RUN authority is separated from the
182	# PLANNED-ORDER manage authority (segregation of duties): running the planning engine is a
183	# planning-controller act, while firming/converting/cancelling a specific proposal is a
184	# planner/buyer act. Read is split too so a viewer can inspect the plan without running it.
185	MFG_MRP_READ = "manufacturing.mrp.read"
186	MFG_MRP_RUN = "manufacturing.mrp.run"

201	    MFG_MRP_READ,
202	    MFG_MRP_RUN,
203	    MFG_PLANNED_ORDER_READ,
204	    MFG_PLANNED_ORDER_MANAGE,
205	    descriptions={
206	        MFG_BOM_READ: "Read bills of materials and their components",
207	        MFG_BOM_MANAGE: "Create, edit and activate bills of materials and their components",
208	        MFG_WORKCENTER_READ: "Read work centres",
209	        MFG_WORKCENTER_MANAGE: "Create and edit work centres",
210	        MFG_ROUTING_READ: "Read routings and their operations",
211	        MFG_ROUTING_MANAGE: "Create, edit and activate routings and their operations",
212	        MFG_PRODUCTION_ORDER_READ: "Read production orders and their components",
213	        MFG_PRODUCTION_ORDER_MANAGE: "Create, edit and cancel production orders",
214	        MFG_PRODUCTION_ORDER_RELEASE: "Release production orders (reserve materials)",
215	        MFG_PRODUCTION_ORDER_EXECUTE: "Issue components to and finish production orders",
216	        MFG_MRP_READ: "Read MRP runs, their planned orders and capacity loads",
217	        MFG_MRP_RUN: "Run material requirements planning",
218	        MFG_PLANNED_ORDER_READ: "Read planned orders",

223	# --- Production-order document type, numbering + docflow links (PLAN 8.2, D-048) ---------------
224	# A production order IS a posted document in the D-012 sense (it registers in core_documents and
225	# claims a gapless number at creation, the orders/deliveries precedent — unlike the 8.1 masters,
226	# which carry no number). The prefix is "MO-" (Manufacturing Order): "PRO-" was an alternative but
227	# "PO-" is already the PURCHASE-order prefix, so a distinct, unambiguous "MO-" avoids any clash.
228	PRODUCTION_ORDER_DOC_TYPE = "manufacturing.production_order"

234	# ISSUE moves and the finished RECEIPT move are inventory documents; manufacturing's flow PUBLISHES
235	# the events and inventory's handler writes these edges (production order → 'issued_to' → ISSUE
236	# move; production order → 'finished_to' → RECEIPT move), as the GR/delivery handlers write their
237	# 'moved_by' edges. A future MRP link (sales order → 'planned_by' → production order) is reserved.
238	PRODUCTION_ORDER_ISSUED_TO_MOVE_LINK = "issued_to"
239	PRODUCTION_ORDER_FINISHED_TO_MOVE_LINK = "finished_to"

242	# PUBLISHES, inventory's handlers create the moves with the WIP offset override.
243	COMPONENTS_ISSUED_EVENT_KEY = "manufacturing.production_order.components_issued"
244	ORDER_FINISHED_EVENT_KEY = "manufacturing.production_order.finished"

246	# PLAN 8.3 (D-049): a planned BUY order's conversion publishes this; procurement's handler creates
247	# the DRAFT requisition (the §5-clean planned-BUY → requisition mechanism, the billing→invoice
248	# precedent — manufacturing never imports procurement service).
249	PLANNED_BUY_CONVERTED_EVENT_KEY = "manufacturing.planned_order.buy_converted"

2	models — so inventory's ``handlers.py`` may import these typed classes (the STRUCTURE §5 events.py
3	allowance: an event carries no behaviour, so a subscriber in another module imports it without any
4	logic).
5	
6	These are the SANCTIONED cross-module mechanism for the production-order → stock-move effects
7	(D-048), mirroring procurement's ``GoodsReceiptPosted`` (6.3, the WIP-offset twin of the GR/IR
8	override) and sales' ``DeliveryShipped``/``ReturnReceived`` (7.3/7.4). Manufacturing OWNS the
9	production-order document; it MUST NOT call inventory's service directly (STRUCTURE §5). So:
10	
11	- ``ComponentsIssued`` (component ISSUE moves → Dr WIP / Cr Inventory): one ``ComponentIssueMove``
12	  per issued component line carries the item, the SOURCE bin, the quantity, optional lot/serial, and
13	  the ``wip_account_id`` — the valuation-offset OVERRIDE every move passes so the costing engine
14	  routes the ISSUE to WIP instead of COGS. The cost of the stock that left is COMPUTED by the
15	  costing engine (moving-average / FIFO), so no unit cost is on the event.
16	- ``OrderFinished`` (finished RECEIPT move → Dr Inventory / Cr WIP): one ``FinishedReceiptMove``
17	  (the parent item entering stock) carries the item, the DESTINATION bin, the finished quantity, the
18	  ``unit_cost`` = accumulated WIP / finished quantity (the goods enter at the WIP-accumulated cost),
19	  optional lot/serial CODES (a RECEIPT may create the master on the fly), and the ``wip_account_id``
20	  override so the costing posts Dr Inventory / Cr WIP.

23	and links the production-order document → 'issued_to'/'finished_to' → move document. The handler
24	shares the session, so the moves + their WIP journals land in the SAME transaction as the
25	issue/finish — all-or-nothing (D-011/D-020): a closed period or insufficient stock rolls the WHOLE
26	issue/finish back.

29	``accumulated_wip_cost``, ``finished_quantity``, status) in that same transaction; the order↔move

1	"""Production-order POSTING flows (PLAN 8.2, D-048) — the heart: issue components to WIP + finish to
2	stock, both through the EVENT BUS (manufacturing publishes; inventory's handlers create the moves
3	with the WIP-offset override; the moves' costing events → finance posts the WIP journals).
4	
5	Split from ``production_orders.py`` at the 400-line cap (the sales delivery_post precedent). The
6	DRAFT lifecycle (create+explode/release/cancel) stays there; the issue/finish POST paths live here.
7	``__init__`` re-exports both halves as one ``service`` surface.
8	
9	THE WIP ACCOUNTING (D-048), the manufacturing↔inventory↔finance seam:
10	
11	- **issue_components** — for each component to issue, PUBLISH ``ComponentsIssued`` → inventory's
12	  handler creates an ISSUE move (from the component's bin, qty, valuation_offset = the WIP account)
13	  → Dr WIP / Cr Inventory at the component's moving-average/FIFO cost. The order raises each
14	  component's ``issued_quantity`` and its ``accumulated_wip_cost`` (by the issued book value — read
15	  pre-publish from inventory's current_unit_cost, which equals the MAV issue cost) and goes
16	  IN_PROGRESS. Over-issue beyond required is a 422 (v1 policy: issued ≤ required). Atomic; a closed
17	  period or insufficient stock rolls the whole issue back (the move guard raises — issue #53: tests
18	  must NOT assert post-failure state on the same session).
19	- **finish_order** — compute the finished unit cost = accumulated WIP / ordered quantity, PUBLISH
20	  ``OrderFinished`` → inventory's handler creates a RECEIPT move (to the finished bin, finished qty,
21	  unit_cost = WIP per unit, valuation_offset = the WIP account) → Dr Inventory / Cr WIP. The order
22	  raises ``finished_quantity`` and DRAINS the absorbed WIP from ``accumulated_wip_cost``. On the
23	  FINAL finish, any residual WIP (over/under-absorption / rounding) is carried on the event so
24	  FINANCE's handler flushes it to the production-variance account — WIP nets to ZERO at completion —
25	  and the order goes FINISHED. Atomic; a closed period rolls the whole finish back.
26	
27	§5: this module imports only inventory/queries + finance/queries + the manufacturing events — never
28	inventory/finance SERVICE (verified). The moves + journals are inventory's/finance's own work,
29	triggered by the events.
30	"""

78	    required of every component is issued from its default bin ("issue all required"). Over-issue
79	    past required is a 422 (v1: issued ≤ required). Atomic — a closed period or insufficient stock
80	    rolls the whole issue back."""
81	    order = await get_production_order(session, tenant_id, order_id)
82	    status = ProductionOrderStatus(order.status)
83	    if status not in (ProductionOrderStatus.RELEASED, ProductionOrderStatus.IN_PROGRESS):
84	        raise ConflictError(
85	            message=f"Components cannot be issued to a {order.status} production order",
86	            code="manufacturing.production_order_not_issuable",
87	            details={"order_id": str(order_id), "status": order.status},
88	        )
89	    wip_account_id = await finance_queries.wip_clearing_account(session, tenant_id)
90	    rows = await production_order_components(session, tenant_id, order_id)
91	    components = {row.line_number: row for row in rows}
92	    move_date = payload.move_date or date.today()
93	    currency_code = await _costing_currency(session, tenant_id)
94	
95	    requested = _resolve_issue_lines(payload, components)
96	    moves: list[ComponentIssueMove] = []
97	    wip_added = Decimal(0)
98	    for component, qty, bin_id, lot_code, serial_code in requested:
99	        _check_over_issue(component, qty)
100	        lot_id, serial_id = await _resolve_issue_tracking(
101	            session, tenant_id, component.component_item_id, lot_code, serial_code
102	        )
103	        # The issued WIP value = the component's current book cost × qty, quantized to the currency
104	        # (the MAV issue posts at avg_unit_cost, so this equals the WIP debit the move will post).
105	        # The finished receipt later enters at accumulated_wip / produced qty, so WIP clears.
106	        unit_cost = await inventory_queries.current_unit_cost(
107	            session, tenant_id, component.component_item_id, order.warehouse_id
108	        )
109	        wip_added += quantize_for_currency(qty * unit_cost, currency_code)
110	        component.issued_quantity = Decimal(component.issued_quantity) + qty
111	        moves.append(
112	            ComponentIssueMove(
113	                item_id=component.component_item_id,
114	                bin_id=bin_id,
115	                quantity=qty,
116	                lot_id=lot_id,
117	                serial_id=serial_id,
118	            )
119	        )

1	"""Manufacturing's cross-module read interface (STRUCTURE §5).
2	
3	Manufacturing sits above inventory/procurement/sales in the dependency order. PLAN 8.2 (production
4	orders) and 8.3 (MRP + rough capacity) read THIS file to resolve an item's active BOM/routing and a
5	work centre's capacity; it is the ONLY manufacturing file those flows import. Keep it thin and
6	stable — it is a contract.
7	
8	The "active" resolvers return the ACTIVE + ``is_default`` version of a BOM/routing for an item (the
9	one the service guarantees is unique per item). ``bom_components`` / ``routing_operations`` return
10	the lines an exploder/scheduler walks. Every function takes an explicit ``tenant_id`` and runs under
11	the caller's tenant context, so the D-007 filter applies on top — ordinary tenant-scoped reads.
12	"""
13	
14	import uuid
15	from decimal import Decimal
16	
17	from sqlalchemy import select
18	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
19

21	    BomStatus,

35	    WorkCenter,
36	)

39	async def get_bom(
40	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, bom_id: uuid.UUID
41	) -> Bom | None:
42	    """The BOM header with ``bom_id`` in the tenant, or None."""
43	    stmt = select(Bom).where(Bom.tenant_id == tenant_id, Bom.id == bom_id)
44	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()

46

48	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
49	) -> Bom | None:
50	    """The ACTIVE default BOM version for an item (D-047), or None if the item has no active
51	    default. The single version 8.2/8.3 explode against. Index-served by (tenant, item_id,
52	    status)."""
53	    stmt = select(Bom).where(
54	        Bom.tenant_id == tenant_id,
55	        Bom.item_id == item_id,
56	        Bom.status == BomStatus.ACTIVE.value,
57	        Bom.is_default.is_(True),

63	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, bom_id: uuid.UUID
64	) -> list[BomComponent]:
65	    """A BOM's direct components, ordered by line_number (the explosion input). One indexed read."""
66	    stmt = (

69	        .order_by(BomComponent.line_number)

83	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
84	) -> Routing | None:

135	
136	
137	async def get_production_order(
138	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_id: uuid.UUID
139	) -> ProductionOrder | None:
140	    """The production-order header with ``order_id`` in the tenant, or None."""
141	    stmt = select(ProductionOrder).where(
142	        ProductionOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id, ProductionOrder.id == order_id
143	    )
144	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
145	
146	
147	async def production_order_components(
148	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_id: uuid.UUID
149	) -> list[ProductionOrderComponent]:
150	    """A production order's exploded component requirements, ordered by line_number (the issue input
151	    + the nested list). One indexed read by (tenant, production_order_id)."""
152	    stmt = (
153	        select(ProductionOrderComponent)
154	        .where(
155	            ProductionOrderComponent.tenant_id == tenant_id,
156	            ProductionOrderComponent.production_order_id == order_id,
157	        )
158	        .order_by(ProductionOrderComponent.line_number)
159	    )
160	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
161	
162	
163	async def order_wip_balance(
164	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_id: uuid.UUID
165	) -> Decimal | None:
166	    """A production order's ACCUMULATED WIP cost (D-048): the running WIP debit raised by each
167	    component issue and consumed at finish. The maintained header figure (not a journal recompute)
168	    so the finish flow derives the finished unit cost from it; the WIP-nets-to-zero SSOT. None if
169	    the order does not exist."""
170	    stmt = select(ProductionOrder.accumulated_wip_cost).where(
171	        ProductionOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id, ProductionOrder.id == order_id
172	    )
173	    value = (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
174	    return Decimal(value) if value is not None else None
175	
176	
177	async def open_production_orders(
178	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID
179	) -> list[ProductionOrder]:
180	    """The OPEN production orders (DRAFT / RELEASED / IN_PROGRESS) — not yet FINISHED or CANCELLED
181	    (PLAN 8.2). 8.3's capacity load + a shop-floor dashboard read these. Index-served by
182	    (tenant, status); ordered by order_number for a stable scan."""
183	    open_statuses = (
184	        ProductionOrderStatus.DRAFT.value,
185	        ProductionOrderStatus.RELEASED.value,
186	        ProductionOrderStatus.IN_PROGRESS.value,
187	    )
188	    stmt = (
189	        select(ProductionOrder)
190	        .where(
191	            ProductionOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id,
192	            ProductionOrder.status.in_(open_statuses),
193	        )
194	        .order_by(ProductionOrder.order_number)
195	    )
196	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
197	
198	
199	# --- MRP supply + planned-order reads (PLAN 8.3, D-049) ------------------------
200	
201	
202	async def open_production_order_supply(
203	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
204	) -> Decimal:
205	    """The UN-FINISHED quantity an item's OPEN production orders will yield (PLAN 8.3) — the
206	    in-house-supply side of the MRP net (the production analogue of procurement's
207	    ``open_incoming_quantity``). Sums ``quantity − finished_quantity`` over the item's
208	    DRAFT/RELEASED/IN_PROGRESS orders (a FINISHED/CANCELLED order yields nothing more). SET-BASED
209	    (no per-order N+1, PERFORMANCE §2): one filtered scan on (tenant, item_id), summed in PYTHON so
210	    the exact-decimal QuantityType round-trips identically on both engines (D-015)."""
211	    open_statuses = (
212	        ProductionOrderStatus.DRAFT.value,
213	        ProductionOrderStatus.RELEASED.value,
214	        ProductionOrderStatus.IN_PROGRESS.value,
215	    )
216	    stmt = select(ProductionOrder.quantity, ProductionOrder.finished_quantity).where(
217	        ProductionOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id,
218	        ProductionOrder.item_id == item_id,
219	        ProductionOrder.status.in_(open_statuses),
220	    )
221	    rows = (await session.execute(stmt)).all()
222	    return sum(
223	        (Decimal(str(qty)) - Decimal(str(finished)) for qty, finished in rows),
224	        Decimal(0),
225	    )
226

229	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, run_id: uuid.UUID
230	) -> MrpRun | None:

232	    stmt = select(MrpRun).where(MrpRun.tenant_id == tenant_id, MrpRun.id == run_id)
233	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()

238	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
239	    mrp_run_id: uuid.UUID,
240	) -> list[PlannedOrder]:
241	    """A run's planned orders, ordered by (level, item) so finished goods (level 0) precede their
242	    components (PLAN 8.3). One indexed read by (tenant, mrp_run_id); the capacity scan + the nested
243	    list read these."""
244	    stmt = (
245	        select(PlannedOrder)
246	        .where(
247	            PlannedOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id,
248	            PlannedOrder.mrp_run_id == mrp_run_id,
249	        )
250	        .order_by(PlannedOrder.level, PlannedOrder.item_id)
251	    )
252	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
253	
254	
255	async def planned_make_supply(
256	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
257	) -> Decimal:
258	    """The quantity an item's still-open FIRMED/CONVERTED planned orders contribute as supply across
259	    ALL runs (PLAN 8.3, the regeneration policy, D-049). A FIRMED/CONVERTED planned order is a
260	    committed replenishment a fresh run must NOT re-propose — so the run nets it as supply.
261	    SET-BASED, summed in Python (D-015)."""
262	    stmt = select(PlannedOrder.quantity).where(
263	        PlannedOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id,
264	        PlannedOrder.item_id == item_id,
265	        PlannedOrder.status.in_(
266	            (PlannedOrderStatus.FIRMED.value, PlannedOrderStatus.CONVERTED.value)
267	        ),
268	    )
269	    rows = (await session.execute(stmt)).all()
270	    return sum((Decimal(str(qty)) for (qty,) in rows), Decimal(0))

1	"""Manufacturing HTTP layer (thin): parse -> call service -> return schema (PLAN 8.1).
2	
3	REST under ``/api/v1/manufacturing``: work-centres (CRUD + filtered list) here, with the BOM surface
4	(``bom_router``) and the routing surface (``routing_router``) mounted as sibling sub-routers at the
5	foot of this file so the whole module stays ONE surface at ``/api/v1/manufacturing`` — the finance
6	journal_router / inventory stock_router include precedent (no second mount in main.py). Every route
7	is guarded by a manufacturing permission key (D-009); writes commit through ``run_in_uow`` (D-011)
8	so audit rows ride the same transaction. The work-centre list is reference data, so it carries a
9	conditional-GET ETag (PERFORMANCE §3 / D-035).
10	"""
11	
12	import uuid
13	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
14	
15	from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request, Response
16	
17	from app.core.conditional import collection_etag, conditional_response, request_fingerprint
18	from app.core.deps import CurrentUserDep, SessionDep
19	from app.core.events import run_in_uow
20	from app.core.pagination import CursorParams, cursor_params, map_page
21	from app.core.rbac import require_permission
22	from app.core.schemas import Page
23	from app.modules.manufacturing import service
24	from app.modules.manufacturing.bom_router import bom_router
25	from app.modules.manufacturing.constants import (
26	    MFG_WORKCENTER_MANAGE,
27	    MFG_WORKCENTER_READ,
28	)
29	from app.modules.manufacturing.models import WorkCenter
30	from app.modules.manufacturing.mrp_router import mrp_router
31	from app.modules.manufacturing.production_order_router import production_order_router
32	from app.modules.manufacturing.routing_router import routing_router
33	from app.modules.manufacturing.schemas import (
34	    WorkCenterCreate,
35	    WorkCenterFilter,
36	    WorkCenterRead,
37	    WorkCenterUpdate,
38	)
39	
40	router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1/manufacturing", tags=["manufacturing"])
41	_CursorParamsDep = Depends(cursor_params)
42	
43	
44	async def _commit[T](session: SessionDep, work: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]]) -> T:
45	    """Run a service call inside the D-011 uow, refreshing the ORM result in the async context so a
46	    sync ``model_validate`` never trips MissingGreenlet (the inventory _commit twin)."""
47	    holder: list[T] = []
48	
49	    async def _work() -> None:
50	        result = await work()
51	        await session.refresh(result)
52	        holder.append(result)
53	
54	    await run_in_uow(session, _work)
55	    return holder[0]
56	
57	
58	@router.get(
59	    "/work-centers",
60	    response_model=Page[WorkCenterRead],
61	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(MFG_WORKCENTER_READ))],
62	)
63	async def list_work_centers(
64	    request: Request,
65	    response: Response,
66	    current: CurrentUserDep,
67	    session: SessionDep,
68	    params: CursorParams = _CursorParamsDep,
69	    is_active: bool | None = None,
70	) -> Page[WorkCenterRead] | Response:
71	    """Conditional-GET supported (D-035): collection ETag over the work-centre reference list; the
72	    active filter folds into the request fingerprint so a filtered 304 is correct."""
73	    filters = WorkCenterFilter(is_active=is_active)
74	    fingerprint = request_fingerprint(params.cursor, params.limit, is_active)
75	    etag = await collection_etag(session, WorkCenter, request_fingerprint=fingerprint)
76	
77	    async def builder() -> Page[WorkCenterRead]:
78	        page = await service.list_work_centers(
79	            session,
80	            current.tenant_id,
81	            filters=filters,
82	            cursor=params.cursor,
83	            limit=params.limit,
84	        )
85	        return map_page(page, WorkCenterRead)
86	
87	    return await conditional_response(request, response, etag, builder)
88	
89	
90	@router.post(
91	    "/work-centers",
92	    response_model=WorkCenterRead,
93	    status_code=201,
94	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(MFG_WORKCENTER_MANAGE))],
95	)
96	async def create_work_center(
97	    payload: WorkCenterCreate, current: CurrentUserDep, session: SessionDep
98	) -> WorkCenterRead:
99	    work_center = await _commit(
100	        session, lambda: service.create_work_center(session, current.tenant_id, payload)
101	    )
102	    return WorkCenterRead.model_validate(work_center)
103	
104	
105	@router.get(
106	    "/work-centers/{work_center_id}",
107	    response_model=WorkCenterRead,
108	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(MFG_WORKCENTER_READ))],
109	)
110	async def get_work_center(
111	    work_center_id: uuid.UUID, current: CurrentUserDep, session: SessionDep
112	) -> WorkCenterRead:
113	    work_center = await service.get_work_center(session, current.tenant_id, work_center_id)
114	    return WorkCenterRead.model_validate(work_center)
115	
116	
117	@router.patch(
118	    "/work-centers/{work_center_id}",
119	    response_model=WorkCenterRead,
120	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(MFG_WORKCENTER_MANAGE))],
121	)
122	async def update_work_center(
123	    work_center_id: uuid.UUID,
124	    payload: WorkCenterUpdate,
125	    current: CurrentUserDep,
126	    session: SessionDep,
127	) -> WorkCenterRead:
128	    work_center = await _commit(
129	        session,
130	        lambda: service.update_work_center(session, current.tenant_id, work_center_id, payload),
131	    )
132	    return WorkCenterRead.model_validate(work_center)
133	
134	
135	# The BOM surface (boms + nested components), the routing surface (routings + nested operations),
136	# the production-order surface (orders + issue/finish actions) and the MRP surface (runs + planned
137	# orders + capacity) are sibling sub-routers mounted here, so the whole module is ONE surface at
138	# /api/v1/manufacturing.
139	router.include_router(bom_router)
140	router.include_router(routing_router)
141	router.include_router(production_order_router)
142	router.include_router(mrp_router)

1	"""Production-order HTTP layer (PLAN 8.2), included into the manufacturing router.
2	
3	A sibling sub-router under the same ``/api/v1/manufacturing`` prefix, mounted by
4	``router.include_router`` in router.py (the bom_router/routing_router precedent — ONE module
5	surface,
6	no second mount in main.py).
7	
8	RBAC (D-009; distinct authorities):
9	  - read by ``manufacturing.production_order.read``;
10	  - create+explode / cancel the order by ``manufacturing.production_order.manage``;
11	  - release (reserve materials) by ``manufacturing.production_order.release``;
12	- issue components + finish to stock by ``manufacturing.production_order.execute`` (both POST stock
13	    + WIP journals — the shop-floor action).
14	
15	Writes commit through ``run_in_uow`` (D-011) so the order + its N stock ISSUE/RECEIPT moves + N WIP
16	journals + the order update commit (or roll back) atomically; the document-creating + issue + finish
17	endpoints are IDEMPOTENT (D-013). The list is O(1) queries + paginated (PERFORMANCE §6).
18	"""
19	
20	import uuid
21	
22	from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
23	
24	from app.core.deps import CurrentUserDep, SessionDep
25	from app.core.events import run_in_uow
26	from app.core.idempotency import Idempotent, IdempotentDep
27	from app.core.pagination import CursorParams, cursor_params, map_page
28	from app.core.rbac import require_permission
29	from app.core.schemas import Page
30	from app.modules.manufacturing import service
31	from app.modules.manufacturing.constants import (
32	    MFG_PRODUCTION_ORDER_EXECUTE,
33	    MFG_PRODUCTION_ORDER_MANAGE,
34	    MFG_PRODUCTION_ORDER_READ,
35	    MFG_PRODUCTION_ORDER_RELEASE,
36	    ProductionOrderStatus,
37	)

39	    FinishOrderRequest,
40	    IssueComponentsRequest,
41	    ProductionOrderComponentRead,
42	    ProductionOrderCreate,
43	    ProductionOrderDetail,
44	    ProductionOrderOperationRead,
45	    ProductionOrderRead,
46	)
47	
48	production_order_router = APIRouter(tags=["manufacturing-production-orders"])
49	
50	_CursorParamsDep = Depends(cursor_params)
51	_CreateIdem = Depends(Idempotent("manufacturing.production_order.create"))
52	_IssueIdem = Depends(Idempotent("manufacturing.production_order.issue"))
53	_FinishIdem = Depends(Idempotent("manufacturing.production_order.finish"))
54	
55	
56	async def _order_detail(
57	    session: SessionDep, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_id: uuid.UUID
58	) -> ProductionOrderDetail:
59	    order = await service.get_production_order(session, tenant_id, order_id)
60	    await session.refresh(order)
61	    components = await service.production_order_components(session, tenant_id, order_id)
62	    operations = await service.production_order_operations(session, tenant_id, order_id)
63	    header = ProductionOrderRead.model_validate(order)
64	    return ProductionOrderDetail(
65	        **header.model_dump(),
66	        components=[ProductionOrderComponentRead.model_validate(c) for c in components],
67	        operations=[ProductionOrderOperationRead.model_validate(o) for o in operations],
68	    )
69	
70	
71	@production_order_router.post(
72	    "/production-orders",
73	    response_model=ProductionOrderDetail,
74	    status_code=201,
75	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(MFG_PRODUCTION_ORDER_MANAGE))],
